intro.html: All ten words describe calm, but calm of different kinds. A serene face and a tranquil lake are peaceful. A composed, unflappable or imperturbable person stays steady when trouble comes, and keeps their equanimity. An impassive, stoic or phlegmatic person shows little feeling at all. A nonchalant person seems not to care.
Peaceful: serene, tranquil. Steady under stress: composed, unflappable, imperturbable, equanimity. Showing little feeling: impassive, stoic, phlegmatic. Unconcerned: nonchalant.
Careful: impassive (showing no feeling) and impassioned (full of feeling) look alike but mean opposite things.

words.ex: At dawn the lake was {serene}, without a ripple or a sound.
words.ctx: The city outside was loud and hurried, but the garden behind the old library was {serene}, with only birdsong and the trickle of a fountain.

mn.text: High on the mountain, Nana Lou sits on a rock and watches the sun go down over the quiet valley. It is a {serene} scene.

scene.alt: A grandmother sits peacefully on a mountain rock watching the sunset as a butterfly floats by.

words.def: quiet and still; free from disturbance
words.ex: By evening the stormy sea had turned {tranquil}.
words.ctx: After a week in the noisy city, the family loved the {tranquil} cabin, where the only sounds at night were crickets and the wind in the pines.

mn.cue: a toy TRAIN and a QUILT: TRAN-QUIL
mn.text: Theo’s toy train sits still on the rug while he sleeps under his warm quilt. The whole room is quiet and {tranquil}.

scene.alt: A toddler sleeps peacefully in bed while a toy train and a teddy bear sit still on the floor.

words.def: in control of your feelings; not flustered
words.ex: Even when the lights went out, the pianist stayed {composed} and went on playing.
words.ctx: Though she was nervous inside, Maya looked {composed} at the interview: she sat up straight, answered slowly and never once fidgeted.

mn.text: When the stage lights flicker during her recital, Lila keeps playing without missing a note. She stays {composed}.

scene.alt: A girl calmly plays the piano on stage while the lights flicker.

words.def: casually unconcerned, as if nothing much matters
words.ex: With a {nonchalant} shrug, Dev said he had probably won the contest.
words.ctx: The rest of the family was frantic about the lost keys, but the cat was {nonchalant}, yawning and stretching in the sunny window as if nothing had happened.
words.etym: From French nonchalant, “not caring”: non (not) + chaloir (to concern), from Latin calere, “to be warm.”
words.note: Nonchalant can praise calm (a nonchalant hero) or criticize carelessness (nonchalant about homework).

mn.text: Everyone is hunting for the lost keys, but the cat just yawns in the sunny window: “I shall not care.” The cat is {nonchalant}.

scene.alt: A worried woman searches for her keys while the cat lounges calmly near them.

words.def: staying calm even in a sudden crisis
words.ex: The {unflappable} pilot landed the plane smoothly in the storm.
words.ctx: When the oven caught fire during the big dinner, the {unflappable} chef simply put it out, opened a window and went on cooking as if nothing had happened.

mn.cue: UN-FLAP-able: never flaps like a chicken
mn.text: The chickens flap and squawk in a panic, but Nana Lou calmly scoops them up one by one. She is {unflappable}.

scene.alt: A calm grandmother gathers up chickens that are flapping around in a panic.

words.def: enduring pain or hardship without complaining
words.ex: The fisherman {stoically} hauled his nets through the freezing rain for hours, without one complaint.
words.ctx: Though the march was long and the food was poor, the {stoic} travelers never grumbled; they simply put one foot in front of the other.
words.etym: From the Stoics, Greek thinkers who taught that a wise person bears hardship calmly; they met in a painted porch called the Stoa.

mn.text: In freezing rain and howling wind, Sven hauls in his nets hour after hour without one complaint. He is {stoic}.

scene.alt: A fisherman in a raincoat steadily hauls in his net in the pouring rain.

words.def: showing no feeling on your face
words.ex: The palace guard stared {impassively} ahead while the children made silly faces at him.
words.ctx: The judge listened to the dramatic story with an {impassive} face, so no one in the courtroom could guess what she was thinking.
words.etym: From im- (not) + passive, in an old sense, “able to feel or suffer,” from Latin pati (to suffer).
words.note: Impassive (showing no feeling) is the opposite of impassioned (full of feeling).

mn.text: The kids tell jokes and make silly faces, but the palace guard’s face does not move a bit. He is {impassive}.

scene.alt: A castle guard keeps a blank face while two children make silly faces at him.

words.def: calmness and evenness of temper, especially under stress
words.ex: Coach Ada met both the big win and the bad loss with {equanimity}.
words.ctx: He accepted the news with {equanimity}; though the trip was canceled, he simply unpacked his bag and suggested a picnic in the park instead.
words.etym: From Latin aequanimitas: aequus (even, equal) + animus (mind).

mn.text: Whether her team wins or loses, Coach Ada’s mood stays perfectly level, like a balanced scale. She meets both with {equanimity}.

scene.alt: A calm coach holding a trophy stands beside a perfectly balanced scale.

words.def: so calm that nothing can upset you
words.ex: Grandpa is {imperturbable}; he reads his paper calmly even in a thunderstorm.
words.ctx: Reporters tried for an hour to rattle the {imperturbable} scientist, but she answered every rude question in the same quiet, even voice.
words.etym: From Latin imperturbabilis: in- (not) + perturbare (to throw into confusion), from turba (turmoil).

mn.text: The wind howls, an umbrella flies past and hats blow away, but Grandpa calmly turns the page of his newspaper. He is {imperturbable}.

scene.alt: A grandfather calmly reads his newspaper on a park bench while a gale blows an umbrella and a hat away.

words.def: calm and unexcitable by nature; slow to show feeling
words.ex: Even as a baby, Sam was {phlegmatic}: he rarely cried, rarely squealed and hardly ever fussed.
words.ctx: Her brother was excitable and loud, but she was {phlegmatic}; even on the day she won the scholarship, she only nodded and said, “Good.”

roots.means: one of the four “humors” of old medicine

words.etym: From Greek phlegma, phlegm: old doctors believed too much of this body fluid made a person sluggish and calm.

mn.cue: a FROG on a MAT: fleg-MAT-ic
mn.text: While the ducks splash and squawk around him, the big frog sits on his lily pad, blinking slowly. Nothing excites him; he is {phlegmatic}.

scene.alt: A big frog sits calmly while two ducks splash and flap around it.

after.html: Stoic adds endurance: a stoic person bears pain or hardship without complaint. Phlegmatic describes a temperament: some people are simply born unexcitable.

items.q: The speaker was impassive. Which describes her?
choices: She showed no feeling at all.
She was very passive and lazy.
items.why: Impassive means showing no emotion. Full of feeling is impassioned, its opposite.

items.q: In “He was so nonchalant about the deadline that he missed it,” the word suggests…
items.why: Nonchalant means casually unconcerned; here it criticizes him for caring too little.

items.q: Which word means a person bears hardship without complaining?
items.why: Stoic adds endurance: bearing pain or hardship without complaint.

items.q: True or false: an unflappable person panics easily.
items.why: False. Unflappable means staying calm even in a crisis.
